newsitem.title: CHINA: Nearly half of Chinese share buyers make money.
newsitem.headline: Nearly half of Chinese share buyers make money.

text.p: About 47 percent of China's investors in the stock market made money in 1996, almost double the rate of 24.1 percent in 1995, according to a survey published in the China Securities newspaper on Friday.
The survey by the China Securities and the Guangfa Securities late last December showed that the rate of profit tended to be influenced by profession, sex, education and time of entering the market.
About 57 percent of owners of private enterprises earned money from stocks while more than 60 percent of students and the unemployed lost money, the newspaper said.
The rate of losses was 50 percent for men and 55.7 percent for women, it said.

About 60 percent of people with an education of primary school or below and 52 percent with college education level made money while 57 percent of people with a middle-school education lost money, it said.
About 46 percent of people who held their shares for at least one year lost money while 68.2 percent of people in the market for less than six months lost money, it said.
